pinyin: bù jiàn tù zǐ bù sā yīng
gloss: You won't catch the eagle until you see the rabbit.
teaser: Ever wondered about the patience required in achieving success? This idiom has the answer.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever wondered about the patience required in achieving success? This idiom has the answer.[break 1s]The phrase is: 不见兔子不撒鹰, bù jiàn tù zǐ bù sā yīng.[break 0.5s]不 (bù) - not[break 0.5s]见 (jiàn) - see[break 0.5s]兔子 (tù zǐ) - rabbit[break 0.5s]不 (bù) - not[break 0.5s]撒 (sā) - release[break 0.5s]鹰 (yīng) - eagle[break 1s]The full idiom again: 不见兔子不撒鹰 means literally 'You won't catch the eagle until you see the rabbit' and figuratively suggests that one should not take action until there is clear evidence or opportunity.[break 1s]Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s]In ancient times, hunters would set their sights on catching rabbits using trained eagles. However, they knew that they couldn't let the eagle fly until they spotted a rabbit; otherwise, it would be a waste of effort. This idiom reflects the idea of waiting for the right moment before taking action, emphasizing patience and strategy in achieving goals.[break 1.5s]Example 1: 你在做这个项目之前，不见兔子不撒鹰。[break 1s]You shouldn't proceed with this project until you see clear evidence of its viability. [break 1s]Example 2: 在投资之前，不见兔子不撒鹰，先做市场调研。[break 1s]Before investing, wait for clear signs and conduct market research first. [break 1s]Example 3: 他总是说要等到有机会才行动，不见兔子不撒鹰。[break 1s]He always says he will act only when there’s an opportunity; patience is key. [break 1s]So, to recap, 不见兔子不撒鹰 means you won't catch the eagle until you see the rabbit, emphasizing the importance of waiting for the right moment. Thank you for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
